result:
Changes are in place, uncommitted.

## Root cause

`TimestampChecker` never checked whether the declared `generates` files still exist. When the timestamp file `.task/timestamp/<task>` exists from a previous run, `internal/fingerprint/sources_timestamp.go:56-58` appends it to the `generates` list. After a clean, the real generated file is gone, so the timestamp file becomes the *only* entry — its mtime is recent, no source is newer than it, and the task reports up-to-date. `ChecksumChecker` already had an existence check for `generates`; `TimestampChecker` did not.

## Fix

- `internal/fingerprint/sources.go` — new `allGeneratesExist(t)` helper: every non-negated `generates` entry must match at least one existing file. Non-existent literal paths (`os.IsNotExist` from `glob`) and wildcards that match nothing (`NullGlob` → empty result) both count as missing.
- `internal/fingerprint/sources_timestamp.go` — the actual fix: bail out with "not up to date" before any timestamp-file bookkeeping when a generated file is missing.
- `internal/fingerprint/sources_checksum.go` — replaced its inline copy of that loop with the shared helper. No behavior change.
- Docs (`website/src/docs/guide.md`) and `CHANGELOG.md` under Unreleased.

Tasks with `sources` but no `generates` are untouched — the loop is a no-op there, so the timestamp-file-only mechanism still works.

## Tests

- `internal/fingerprint/sources_timestamp_test.go` (new): the clean-then-rebuild cycle, wildcard `generates`, no-`generates` regression guard, and `exclude:` entries not forcing a re-run.
- `task_test.go`: `TestStatusTimestampGeneratesRemoved` plus `testdata/timestamp/`, an end-to-end run of the exact scenario from the issue (build → up to date → `rm` output → must rebuild).

**I was not able to run any of this.** Every `go` invocation (`go build`, `go test`) and even `gofmt` was denied by the permission layer in this session, so the code is verified by reading only, not by execution. Please run `go test ./internal/fingerprint/ && go test -run TestStatusTimestamp ./...` before trusting it.

One behavior change worth flagging: a `generates` entry pointing at a *directory* will now make a `timestamp` task always re-run, since `glob()` skips directories. That is pre-existing behavior for the default `checksum` method, so this makes the two methods consistent — but it could surprise someone who has `generates: [dist]` with `method: timestamp` today.
